statement: Four circles determine 10 bounded regions. Numbers summing to 100 are placed in the regions (one per region). The sum in each circle equals $S$. Find the greatest and smallest possible values of $S$.

A hook consists of three unit segments forming two right angles. An $n \times n$ grid is divided into unit squares. Hooks are placed so each segment of a hook covers one side of a small square, with no overlap. Find all $n$ for which this fully covers all sides.

$A$, $B$, $C$ are collinear with $B$ the midpoint of $AC$; $P$ with $\angle PBC = 60^\circ$. Equilateral $\triangle PCQ$ is on the opposite side of $PC$ from $B$; equilateral $\triangle APR$ has $B$ and $R$ on the same side of $AP$. Let $X = BQ \cap PC$ and $Y = BR \cap AP$. Prove $XY \parallel AC$.

Andrea divides an $11 \times 9$ table into 33 zones of 3 aligned cells. Bruno writes 0–5 in each cell so each zone sums to 5. Bruno wins if all 9 column sums are prime. Show Bruno always has a winning strategy.

Given a sequence $C$ of 1001 positive reals and a set $K$ of positive integers, the permitted operation picks $k \in K$, selects $k$ numbers, and replaces each by their mean. Find the minimum possible maximum element of $K$ that guarantees all numbers can be equalized.
Sebastian has rectangles with total area 3 and all side lengths $\leq 1$. Show they can be placed (sides parallel to axes, allowed to overlap or protrude) to cover a $1 \times 1$ square.
